text:
“Do you know why I pulled you over?” is not small talk.

It is the one question in a traffic stop that invites you to agree to something before anyone has accused you of anything. You do not have to guess, and you do not have to answer it.

Silence is your right, but you have to claim it out loud. Just going quiet is not enough — say it: “I'm using my right to remain silent.”

Berghuis v. Thompkins, 560 U.S. 370 (2010); Salinas v. Texas, 570 U.S. 178 (2013)

Amparo has a free drill for exactly this moment — the Admission Trap. Three minutes, no account, English or Spanish.
